title: IT Act ss. 4 & 5 — Charge of income-tax & Scope of total income (IT Act ss. 4-5)

content.overview: Section 4 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 charges income-tax for the assessment year on the total income of the previous year of every person. Section 5 defines the scope of total income by residence: a resident is taxed on Indian and foreign income, with the resident-but-not-ordinarily-resident limit, and a non-resident is taxed on income received or accruing in India. Charge and scope are separate. Section 4 imposes the tax. Section 5 decides which income enters the total.
content.glance: IT Act ss. 4 & 5 — Charge of income-tax & Scope of total income (IT Act ss. 4-5). Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Decide residence, then apply section 5, then charge under section 4. Do not invent a rate.

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: Section 4 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 charges income-tax for the assessment year on the total income of the previous year of every person. Section 5 defines the scope of total income by residence: a resident is taxed on Indian and foreign income, with the resident-but-not-ordinarily-resident limit, and a non-resident is taxed on income received or accruing in India.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Charge and scope are separate. Section 4 imposes the tax. Section 5 decides which income enters the total.
essentialIngredients: Receipt or accrual in India for a non-resident
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 4 is the charge. The rate comes from the Finance Act. Section 5(1) brings in all income of a resident, received or accruing anywhere, subject to the not-ordinarily-resident rule in the section. Section 5(2) limits a non-resident to income received or deemed received in India, or accruing or arising or deemed to accrue or arise in India. Deeming provisions elsewhere can expand Indian accrual.
examples: A non-resident earns the same rent abroad and it is not received in India.
Section 5(2) does not include it unless a deeming provision applies.
enhancement.problemApplication: Decide residence, then apply section 5, then charge under section 4. Do not invent a rate.
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Rates and notifications are not frozen in this note.
